precepts.text: Joseph is blessed with the precious things put forth by the moon.
precepts.point: The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
Moses blesses Joseph: “Blessed of the Lord be his land, for the precious things of heaven, for the dew, and for the deep that coucheth beneath,” “And for the precious fruits brought forth by the sun, and for the precious things put forth by the moon”. Joseph's sons, Ephraim and Manasseh, dwell on islands: the Puerto Ricans and the Cubans, among others.

The precious things of heaven are the rain; the deep that coucheth beneath is the oceans that give riches beneath the waters. There are certain fruits brought forth by the sun, and certain things that come forth only by moonlight on those islands, like the coquí frog, which is nocturnal and comes out especially under the moonlight, making its noise.

That blessing points to the moon at its peak, what they call the full moon today, which is actually the new moon. That is what leads into Ecclesiasticus 43:6: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.”

precepts.text: The feasts of the Lord, starting with the Sabbath, are his appointed times.
precepts.point: The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
The moon serves “in her season for a declaration of times”. Leviticus 23 shows what those times are: “Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of the Lord, which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.” Convocations means gatherings.

The first holy day God tells Moses to list is the Sabbath: “Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest”, instituted from Genesis 2. Then: “These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.” He did not say seasons for the Sabbath, because the Sabbath is all year round. The ones that follow are seasonal holy days.

“In the fourteenth day of the first month at even is the Lord’s passover”, in the spring. Then the feast of unleavened bread on the fifteenth day; Pentecost, counting fifty days; “In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets”, which is the seventh new moon celebration; the day of atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month; and “The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles”.

So the “declaration of times” is the high holy days. “From the moon is the sign of feasts”: every feast is counted from the new moon, when it is in its brightness, because that is how it was in the kingdom.

precepts.text: Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of what follows.
precepts.point: The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
What is “a sign of the world”? One answer given from 2 Esdras 6:9, that Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of the world that follows, is that the sign of the world goes into our rulership and their destruction. That is not 100% wrong, and it should not be discounted.

The fuller understanding is this. The moon at its full is when we were in our full power and full understanding, in the kingdom. As it wanes and gets dark, it is us going into captivity, into full darkness. And once it gets back to fullness, it is us going back into our glory, back into the kingdom. That is the passing from Esau's world to Jacob's.

The moon's phases represent the stages the world is in: “a light that decreaseth in her perfection”, “increasing wonderfully in her changing”. And in the kingdom it will not wane again: “the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun”, and the sun has no phases. When Jacob's world follows Esau's, there is no going back into darkness.

precepts.text: Darkness covers the earth and gross darkness the people until Israel's light comes.
precepts.point: The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
“Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.” Arise means wake up; shine means teach; and the light that is come is Christ, who said, I am the light. “For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people”. We are in the grossest of darkness; we have lost our heritage and lost everything. When you see the moon dark, that is what it represents: darkness has covered the whole world.

Psalms 82 shows the same darkness. “God standeth in the congregation of the mighty; he judgeth among the gods.” The little g is us. Asaph, with the Holy Spirit upon him, records what we did wrong as the gods of the earth: “How long will ye judge unjustly, and accept the persons of the wicked?” We were to defend the poor and fatherless and deliver the needy, but “they walk on in darkness: all the foundations of the earth are out of course.” “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.” “But ye shall die like men”: our godhood was taken from us. “Arise, O God, judge the earth: for thou shalt inherit all nations.”

Something in the heavens is out of course because of our sins. God made “two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night”. But in the kingdom, Isaiah 30:26: “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The sun has no phases; in the kingdom the moon, the sign of the world, will not go dark again. And the sun we call so bright is not bright at all next to that.

Binding up the breach is Amos 9:11: “In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and close up the breaches thereof”, gathering the twelve tribes of Israel back again. That is when Isaiah 60:1 is fulfilled: our light is come, the moon is back at its fullness, and Israel is back in the kingdom.

precepts.text: Look upon the rainbow and praise Him that made it; the hands of the Most High bended it.
precepts.point: The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.

note.label: Genesis 9: The Laws Before Moses and the Covenant of the Bow

precepts.why:
The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth. “Look upon the rainbow, and praise him that made it; very beautiful it is in the brightness thereof. It compasseth the heaven about with a glorious circle, and the hands of the most High have bended it.”

His hands bended it. When you see the bow you are to praise Him that made it, and remember the covenant it stands for.

precepts.text: The moon serves for a declaration of times, and from the moon is the sign of feasts; the month is called after her name.
precepts.point: If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

note.label: Leviticus 23: The Feasts of the Lord

precepts.why:
“In the seventh month, in the first day of the month, shall ye have a sabbath, a memorial of blowing of trumpets.” The first day of the month is the new moon, so the memorial of blowing of trumpets is a new moon; the seventh new moon is the special one, and that one is called the memorial of blowing of trumpets.

The Most High “made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world. From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.” The moon is needed to calculate the feasts. “The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing”: the new moon starts the new month, and she increases through her phases.

If the new moon falls on a seventh day Sabbath there is absolutely no cooking; the only day that permits cooking on the Sabbath is the Passover.

precepts.text: The moon declares the times and seasons and is the sign of feasts; her cycle marks the beginnings of the months.
precepts.point: The beginnings of the months are marked by the moon: the Most High made the moon to serve in her season for a declaration of times, a light that decreaseth in her perfection and then increaseth in her changing, and the month is called after her name. When the light is full again, that is the new moon.

note.label: Numbers 10: The Silver Trumpets and the Order of the Journeys

precepts.why:
The trumpets were blown “in the day of your gladness, and in your solemn days, and in the beginnings of your months”, over the burnt offerings and the peace offerings, “for a memorial before your God.” The beginnings of the months are marked by the moon.

“He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world. From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection. The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing.” The moon declares the times and seasons and is the sign of the feasts; her cycle marks the beginnings of the months. Her light decreases in her perfection and then increases in her changing, and when the light is full again, that is the new moon.

The feast days must be a glad moment even to this day. Coming to congregate with your brothers and sisters grudgingly is one of the reasons Israel went into captivity: we were not glad to do what the Most High said.

precepts.text: How shall we be able to magnify him, for he is great above all his works?
precepts.point: I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it; and I will wait on thy name, for it is good before thy saints.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why: “I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it”. “How shall we be able to magnify him? for he is great above all his works.” He is great above all his works, so how can we magnify him enough? David's answer is to praise him for ever and wait on his name, for it is good before his saints.

precepts.text: When you glorify the Most High, exalt him as much as you can, for he far exceeds; put forth all your strength and be not weary, for you can never go far enough.
precepts.point: I will praise thee for ever, because thou hast done it; and I will wait on thy name, for it is good before thy saints.

note.label: Psalm 52: The Boasting Man of Sin Revealed

precepts.why:
“When ye glorify the Lord, exalt him as much as ye can; for even yet will he far exceed: and when ye exalt him, put forth all your strength, and be not weary; for ye can never go far enough.” Exalt the Most High as much as you can, for he far exceeds it; put forth all your strength and be not weary, for you can never go far enough.

That is why David says “I will praise thee for ever”. Praise for ever is the only fitting measure for one great above all his works, and waiting on his name is good before his saints.

precepts.text: The moon marks the seasons and the appointed feasts.
precepts.point: He makes darkness and it is night, wherein the beasts of the forest and the young lions seek their meat from God; the night belongs to the beasts, the day belongs to man who goes to his labor until evening.

note.label: Psalm 104: The Most High Clothed with Majesty over Creation

precepts.why:
“He appointed the moon for seasons”. Ecclesiasticus gives the reason: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.”

“From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.” The moon does not only mark the seasons; it marks the appointed feasts of the Most High. That is the office he gave it in the creation, alongside the sun that “knoweth his going down”, the darkness he makes for the beasts of the forest and the day he gives to man for his labour until the evening.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why: It just said the armies which were in heaven followed him. “The month is called after her name, increasing wonderfully in her changing”, being the moon, “being an instrument of the armies above.” Y’all see what the moon is? The moon is an instrument of the armies above. It’s a base.

note.label: Passover: a Celebration of Deliverance From Oppression

precepts.why:
“And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years”. Notice it keeps saying lights, lights: “let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so.”

“And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day”: that’s the sun. “The lesser light to rule the night”: that’s the moon. This is why Israelites have different dates on the high holidays: they have yet to understand that when God made two great lights, that was the sun and what the world calls the full moon. Two great lights means exactly what it says. It doesn’t mean when it’s dark the moon was out; it doesn’t mean a quarter moon, a half moon, a sliver of a moon. It means the moon at full capacity, in its perfection: the light that decreaseth in her perfection.

“He made the stars also. And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth, And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God saw that it was good. And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.” You got to ask some of the camps: when God created two great lights, did he make the moon black? It doesn’t make any sense. We were all under that understanding at one time, when we came into the truth, but the Lord has henceforth opened our eyes to what the scriptures are saying.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “From the moon is the sign of feasts.” A sign of what? Of feasts. The moon is a sign of feasts. It goes on, “a light that decreaseth in her perfection”, but the part wanted is that the moon is the sign of feasts: it is what tells the feasts that are proclaimed in their seasons.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.” The moon serves in her season, for a declaration of times, and the moon is a sign of the world. Remember: the sun rules by day, mercy endures forever; the moon rules by night, mercy endures forever. So what world is she a sign of?

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
Remember: the sun is Jacob, the moon the mother, the eleven stars the brothers. “The sun when it appeareth, declaring at his rising a marvellous instrument, the work of the most High.” The sun declares at his rising. So the sun is a man.

That does not mean to go crazy and worship the sun. That is what happened to us in the first place: we knew what this meant, and we started bugging out over it. Jacob considered what Joseph said because he knew what the sun represented, and the moon too.

It is a marvellous instrument, a marvellous sign. Remember Genesis, that great light: when the sun shines, that is its instrument in its perfection. And it is not perfect when it is going down; it is perfect when it is coming up.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
“He made the moon also to serve in her season.” Put it beside Jacob’s words: shall I the sun, and your mother the moon, and your brothers the eleven stars serve you, Joseph? So the sun is the man and the moon is the woman, the husband and the wife, and the stars are the children.

And he made her “for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.”

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
“The pride of the height, the clear firmament, the beauty of heaven, with his glorious shew; The sun when it appeareth, declaring at his rising a marvellous instrument, the work of the most High.”

“At noon it parcheth the country”: it makes the earth real hot at noon time, “and who can abide the burning heat thereof?” That noonday is the day that burns as an oven.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: So the thought isn’t lost: the moon is a light, a sign of the world. “But Israel shall be saved in the Lord with an everlasting salvation: ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end.” World without end. So the moon is a sign of the world without end: Israel.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: How do we know the moon in her glory is when she is full? “Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again”: he was righteous, “and in his days fortified the temple.” In his days, during Simon II’s reign as the high priest, the temple was fortified.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “He was as the morning star in the midst of a cloud, and as the moon at the full.” The morning star: that is the sun. And he was as the moon at the full. What does that mean? Read on to verse 11.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
“When he put on the robe of honour, and was clothed with the perfection of glory.” That is how we know: the moon at the full is the perfection of glory. When it is full, it is new.

Somebody used that scripture trying to contradict us, but they did not read it properly. It is describing the moon fully full of light, the new moon: full of light, the way it was created. When the moon is perfect, when it is new, it is in its glory. That is how the priest was.

“When he went up to the holy altar, he made the garment of holiness honourable”, because he was righteous. He stood by the hearth of the altar “as a young cedar in Libanus”, in Lebanon, “and as palm trees compassed they him round about. So were all the sons of Aaron in their glory”: like the moon at the full, like the morning star, at noon.

When you are full of light, you are in your glory. Keep that in mind.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
Children of light. “This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” “Turn thee, O Jacob, and take hold of it”: take hold of the commandments, the Bible.

“Walk in the presence of the light thereof”: hold your lamps, like the virgins, “that thou mayest be illuminated.” Illuminated: full of light, like the moon.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “But the love of the Lord passeth all things for illumination”: illumination is enlightenment. “He that holdeth it, whereto shall he be likened?” He will be likened to the full moon and the sun.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after ye were illuminated, ye endured a great fight of afflictions.” Ye were illuminated: in other places it is ‘enlightened’, the same word. Enlightenment.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “O Lord, thou spakest from the beginning of the creation, even the first day, and saidst thus; Let heaven and earth be made; and thy word was a perfect work.”

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: Back here again for a reason: “Upon the fourth day thou commandedst that the sun should shine, and the moon give her light, and the stars should be in order.” The sun is the bridegroom; now we are going to deal with the moon, and her light.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
Why does she decrease from her perfection? The moon is a sign of the world, which is Israel. “Yet I had planted thee a noble vine, wholly a right seed”: you were in your glory, noble and glorious, holy, righteous, new.

“How then art thou turned into the degenerate plant of a strange vine unto me?” We became degenerate. What does degenerate mean? When you go backwards, when you decrease. We went from being a noble vine, full of light, and degenerated into darkness. Now you are starting to catch on to what the moon is for. You ever heard the term? You all are a bunch of degenerates.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
The sun, the moon, the woman in her sorrow for seven days, and the child clean on the eighth day when he is circumcised: that has not been forgotten. The sun represents the bridegroom, Christ, the husband. So who is the moon?

“Son of man, when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it by their own way and by their doings.” We went from being full of light to full of darkness. “Their way was before me as the uncleanness of a removed woman.” How long is she removed?

“Wherefore I poured my fury upon them for the blood that they had shed upon the land, and for their idols wherewith they had polluted it: And I scattered them among the heathen, and they were dispersed through the countries: according to their way and according to their doings I judged them.”

So he removed us as an unclean woman, and we read before how long a woman is unclean.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
Now we read about her increase. The hand of the Lord set Ezekiel “in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”, and “they were very dry.” “Son of man, can these bones live?”

“Behold, I will cause breath to enter into you, and ye shall live: And I will lay sinews upon you, and will bring up flesh upon you”: knowledge of identity, the seeking of identity, “and cover you with skin, and put breath in you”: understanding who you are, “and ye shall live; and ye shall know that I am the Lord.” You shall remember yourselves. This goes right back to the fringes again: learning who you are.

“The bones came together, bone to his bone”, the sinews and flesh came up and the skin covered them, “but there was no breath in them”: no understanding yet, just the seeking of identity. This goes into the turbulent 60s, Malcolm, Martin.

“Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain.” We were spiritually destroyed, killed. Then watch the increasing: “the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army.”

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “And after seven days”: seven days, remember, that is the time you are unclean. “The world, that yet awaketh not”, that was asleep, “shall be raised up”: an exceeding great army. “And that shall die that is corrupt.” After a while we are going to get out of here and get the kingdom.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: Regarding the waxing, which is where we are right now: what happened with Christ is happening with us; the light is increasing. “And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, filled with wisdom: and the grace of God was upon him.” Waxed means increased.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
The same with his cousin John: “And the child grew, and waxed strong in spirit, and was in the deserts till the day of his shewing unto Israel.”

So we are waxing with wisdom: that is the increase, going back to the fullness, to being new. The newness represents the new body, the circumcision without hands. That is the full moon: us in our glory, shining as the morning star, as the moon at the full, in perfection. The new body, the new moon: it is the same thing.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
“These are the two olive trees, and the two candlesticks standing before the God of the earth.” This goes into the two kingdoms, and also two figures.

“Fire proceedeth out of their mouth, and devoureth their enemies”: that goes to Elijah. “These have power to shut heaven, that it rain not in the days of their prophecy”: Elijah. “And have power over waters to turn them to blood”: Moses. “And to smite the earth with all plagues, as often as they will.” We will gain that power again: as we reach that fullness, we are going to do the same thing our forefathers did.

“The beast that ascendeth out of the bottomless pit shall make war against them, and shall overcome them, and kill them.” That goes back to Ezekiel 37, the slain, the bones in that valley: us being enslaved and conquered. “Their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”, Babylon, “which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.”

The nations “shall see their dead bodies three days and an half”: 350 years without knowledge and wisdom, dead, the valley of dry bones. They “shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves”, because it is spiritual. “They that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry, and shall send gifts one to another; because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth”: we ruled.

“And after three days and an half”, after 350 years, in the midst of those seven days, in the midst of that week, “the Spirit of life from God entered into them”: waxing, increase. “And they stood upon their feet”: increase. “And great fear fell upon them which saw them”, because of what we are going to do in verse six, when we smite them with plagues.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
That is the increase. “He that giveth his mind to the law of the most High, and is occupied in the meditation thereof, will seek out the wisdom of all the ancient, and be occupied in prophecies.” He keeps the sayings of the renowned men, seeks out the secrets of grave sentences, and is “conversant in dark parables.”

“He shall serve among great men, and appear before princes”: he talks with the ambassadors, the prime ministers. That is what is happening with us. “He will travel through strange countries”: their line has gone forth through the earth.

“When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks unto the Lord in his prayer. He shall direct his counsel and knowledge, and in his secrets shall he meditate.”

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
“Yet have I more to say, which I have thought upon; for I am filled as the moon at the full.” Filled as the moon at the full, because of verse six: “he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding.” You cannot get around this.

Understanding is the moon, and it is at its full when the Holy Spirit comes into us: like the moon at the full, meaning when it is new. The moon is full when it is new. The heathens serve the devil, so they are completely opposite of us: they keep the new moon as a black moon, because they are darkness itself, and so is their god.

We are children of light; we deal with light. The one time we deal with the darkness is when the Lord said the evening and the morning were the first day: the day starts at night. But for keeping the feast days, he says use the light to keep my commandments, because you are children of light. He gave light for wisdom both ways, physically and spiritually.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
After the seventh day, after that seventh cycle, you get a new moon. “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the Lord, so shall your seed and your name remain.” The new moon represents a new heaven and a new earth, where we are filled at the full.

“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” We are going to be keeping the sabbaths and new moons in the kingdom.

“And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me”: those are the foolish virgins that did not have their oil for their lamps, “for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched.”

The Sabbath represents rest, eternal rest: no more work and no more oppression for us; somebody else does the work. In the kingdom we are going to be celebrating the day the Lord gives us rest.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
The waning and the waxing: “How is the gold become dim!” What does gold normally do? It shines. It was light, and now it is not light any more; it is dimming. “How is the most fine gold changed!” Who is he referring to? “The stones of the sanctuary are poured out in the top of every street”: when the Babylonians attacked us.

“The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold, how are they esteemed as earthen pitchers, the work of the hands of the potter!” We lost our shine.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
Now in these last days we are gaining our shine again. “Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun”: as great as the light of the sun, in its original glory. There will be no more night, so the moon has no reason to go into darkness again; it will be bright all the time. The sun and moon represent us: we will be full of light, and likewise the moon will be full of light.

“And the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the Lord bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.” The bright sun and the bright moon symbolize the healing and deliverance of our people. The sun is the groom, Christ; the bride is Israel. Israel is the moon.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why:
“And it shall come to pass in that day, that the light shall not be clear, nor dark: But it shall be one day which shall be known to the Lord, not day, nor night: but it shall come to pass, that at evening time it shall be light.” At evening time it shall be light because the moon will be just as bright as the sun, the night as bright as the day. This goes into the Lord’s return and into the kingdom.

“In that day, that living waters shall go out from Jerusalem.” And “the Lord shall be king over all the earth”: that is how you know it is the kingdom. “In that day shall there be one Lord, and his name one.” There will not be a bunch of names; we are all going to know the name of the Lord and of his son, both their names, completely, no confusion.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

precepts.why: “For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ: Who shall change our vile body”: our unclean body, “that it may be fashioned like unto his glorious body”, like that sun at noon and the moon at the full, “according to the working whereby he is able even to subdue all things unto himself.” We are going to be new, like he is new.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: “For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world is the world during the time of Adam: back then it brought forth immortality. That is the moon in her perfection, bright and full.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: “For look how much the world shall be weaker through age, so much the more shall evils increase upon them that dwell therein.” Weaker through age means time: the more time goes by on this earth, the more evils will increase. That is the light decreasing from her perfection.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: “For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.” The earth is going to be in total darkness, just like a phase of the moon when it goes black.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
“For the world hath lost his youth, and the times begin to wax old.” “For the world is divided into twelve parts”: the angel is telling Ezra to look at the earth like a clock. Twelve parts on the clock, “and the ten parts of it are gone already”: ten o’clock, gone already, “and half of a tenth part”: that’s the 10:30 mark.

This was back then, during the time of Ezra, the time of Persia and Media, that the angel was telling him this. “And there remaineth that which is after the half of the tenth part”: from that time, all that’s left is an hour and a half. That is the moon as a declaration of times.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
“Then did I consider these things, and they all were made through me alone, and through none other”: that’s Christ speaking. “By me also they shall be ended, and by none other.” Ezra asks, “What shall be the parting asunder of the times? or when shall be the end of the first”: when shall be the end of the first world, “and the beginning of it that followeth?”, the beginning of the world that follows.

“From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him, Jacob’s hand held first the heel of Esau. For Esau is the end of the world, and Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth.” Esau is the last ruling empire. That’s what it means: Esau is the end of the world.

When you hear some Israelites out there say Esau is the Arabs, no, that’s wrong. If Esau is the Arabs, that means we got to go into captivity again, and that makes no damn sense. What the hell wrong with you? The Bible says Esau will go to the moon; I don’t see no damn Arabs going up there. That’s why you don’t listen to them. Some of you women are all over the place; you listen to everybody, simple as hell. Stop listening to them; you’re gonna get lost.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”: that’s the other nations. “Other question, Esdras, ask thou not.” And in case some of you watching online dispute what’s being said: shut up and listen.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: “Then saw I a dream, and, behold, there came up from the sea an eagle, which had twelve feathered wings, and three heads.” The question is, who was this? Obadiah answers it: Edom, whose symbol is the eagle. Then back here: “And I saw, and, behold, she spread her wings over all the earth, and all the winds of the air blew on her”. He’s talking about the eagle in all her forms: Esau, the end of the world.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why:
“The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”: concerning who? Edom. “We have heard a rumour from the Lord”, and the heathen are called to “rise up against her in battle”: that’s NATO. They’re prophesied to rise up against America. “Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.” Esau greatly despised.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”: put the Caucasus mountains on the screen. These are the Caucasus mountains of Georgia, Russia, where the Khazars dwelt that we read about at the beginning of today’s lesson, the Khazars of Edomite stock that make up the Jews of today. “Whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?” To say who shall bring me down to the ground, you got to have power.

“Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars”: when they landed on the moon in 1969 they said the eagle has landed, and they have mementos all throughout the country in regards to that. So Esau’s symbol is the eagle, the same eagle Ezra saw come up from the sea.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

precepts.why: “And I beheld, and lo, as it were a roaring lion”: this roaring lion is Christ, “chased out of the wood”, meaning it ran out of the woods. “And I saw that he sent out a man’s voice unto the eagle”: the voice that’s coming out is the voice of the prophets. “Hear thou, I will talk with thee, and the Highest shall say unto thee, Art not thou it that remainest of the four beasts, whom I made to reign in my world, that the end of their times might come through them?” That the end of their times might come through them: this eagle would bring about the end of this time. Esau is the end of the world, the moon gone dark.

note.label: Day of Atonement

note.label: Day of Atonement

note.label: The End Of PAX Americana

A light that decreaseth in her perfection: when God created the moon, it was a light. When it is perfect is when it is a light, when it is new; after it is new, then it decreases. Tonight when you look up in the sky and see a bright light, that is the new moon.

note.label: The End Of PAX Americana

points: The month is called after her name: the word month derives from the word moon. Increasing wonderfully in her changing: after it decreases, it increases. Being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven.

note.label: The End Of PAX Americana

What is called the full moon is the new moon, when its light is at its peak.
Its phases show Israel's history: full light in the kingdom, darkness in captivity, and full light again when the kingdom returns.
The moon is an instrument of the armies above.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

note.label: Mind Control & The Power Of Prayer

note.label: Mind Control & The Power Of Prayer

note.label: Mind Control & The Power Of Prayer

points: Many times we get emails asking why the Passover dates are different amongst the Israelite camps. Here’s the main reason why many camps have different Passover dates than us: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.”

note.label: Passover: a Celebration of Deliverance From Oppression

points: “From the moon is the sign of feasts”: see that, the feasts are set by the moon. Then “a light that decreaseth in her perfection”. A light: that’s the key term. The moon is a light that decreases from her perfection.

note.label: Passover: a Celebration of Deliverance From Oppression

points: “The month is called after her name”: that’s where the word month comes from; month means moon. “Increasing wonderfully in her changing, being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven”.

When you look at the moon phases, the new moon is what society calls the full moon. It decreases wonderfully in her changing till it’s dark, then it increases in her changing, which goes back to the full.

note.label: Passover: a Celebration of Deliverance From Oppression

points: Back to it, in case you got lost: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.” The sign of the world: that is it.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: From the top again: “The pride of the height, the clear firmament, the beauty of heaven, with his glorious shew”. Then: “From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.”

She decreases in her perfection. When is the moon in her perfection? When she is full. She decreases when she is full: when she is new, in her glory, the way she was made. Her perfection is the perfection of her light, her glory.
Read seven first. What they do is read eight first and read above it; no, seven goes first, then eight. You failed eight years ago and you are going to fail again.
Why does she decrease from her perfection? Remember, the moon is a sign of the world, which is Israel.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “From the moon is the sign of feasts, a light that decreaseth in her perfection.”

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: “The month is called after her name”: the word month comes from the word moon. “Increasing wonderfully in her changing”: she begins to increase wonderfully when she is in darkness, after she has decreased. “Being an instrument of the armies above, shining in the firmament of heaven”: that is her glory, when she shines.

There are eight phases of the moon. Start from the new moon, in perfection, full of light; then she begins to degenerate. Going down, that is called the waning: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, and then waxing, until on the eighth you are back where you were before. Eighth day, you are clean again, full of light again. You start off full of light, go through that phase of uncleanness, the removed woman, and begin to wax, like that exceeding great army, until you are back where you began: children of light all over again. That is why we start from the top, not from the bottom.
What they call the dark moon is just darkness. You are using darkness to observe light.

note.label: Thankskilling Get Away: A Sign of The World

points: We are in some dark times, and the Lord has been showing us, but we don’t catch it. “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times”: the moon serves in a season for a declaration of time.

“And a sign of the world”: that’s the part right there. The moon symbolizes a sign of the world we live in. Put up the phases of the moon: what they call a full moon is actually the new moon. It goes from bright, and phases all the way to dark, decreasing; then it begins to increase again.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “A light that decreaseth in her perfection.” The new moon is bright, in her perfection. When was the earth in its perfection? During the time of Adam. Then it begins to decrease, and darkness begins to cover it till it gets black.
When the moon is dark, that represents sin and Satan and all the wickedness, Edom and all the wickedness that we see taking place.

So what have we learned? The moon is a declaration of times, a sign of the world; it’s symbolic of the world. It started out in its perfection and it decreased until it gets dark, as we read in Isaiah 60:2. Then after Esau, who comes? Brothers, Jacob, like we read, and it begins to go right back. That’s what the moon symbolizes.

note.label: Lazarus and the Lake of Fire

points: “He made the moon also to serve in her season for a declaration of times, and a sign of the world.” The moon is what is used to tell the seasons. That is how you are able to tell time, through the moon.

note.label: War With The Beast: Death & Persecution

points: “From the moon is the sign of feasts”: that is how you know when the feast day is coming. And when the moon was created it was “a light that decreaseth in her perfection.” Not a light that increases, a light that decreases. When she is perfect she is a light, and then she decreases.

Today the world has taught our people that the moon is new when it is dark. But when the moon was created, it was a light. That was done to confuse our feast days: if the moon is what tells the feast days, and they throw that off, everything is off.

note.label: War With The Beast: Death & Persecution

points: “The month is called after her name.” The word month is derived from the word moon, “increasing wonderfully in her changing.”
